content:
Hi, with the help of OpenAI I have crafted a Lean formalization of Rosser–Schoenfeld’s Theorem 12.
The formalization is available for review on Github:
https://github.com/hakonlonmo/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/tree/rs12-formalization
Under my instruction and supervision, OpenAI successfully verified Theorem 12 with a sorry free audit.

With an interest for math, I find it inspiring that one can prove theorems with Lean. My suggestion is that even though both the design and implementation work was done by OpenAI, the result may be of use to the community. Therefore I share the results.
I would highly appreciate feedback if this kind of formalization is useful, or if it can be considered AI garbage.

Attached is the complete explanation of the proof.
rosser_schoenfeld_theorem12_formalization_rewrite.pdf

You can submit this as a node to the IEANTN https://github.com/teorth/IEANTN (probably something like RosserSchoenfeld1962.v1 given your description; there is already a rudimentary RosserSchoenfeld.v1 node but it is based on a later 1975 paper). Hopefully just pointing your agent to the repository will allow it to understand the network structure, and what kind of node would be appropriate to add to it, and how to format your submission to be compatible with the network.

Thanks. I have created PR 125 - Formalize Rosser–Schoenfeld 1962 equation (3.35)
https://github.com/teorth/IEANTN/pull/125

  • Adds RosserSchoenfeld1962.v1.equation_3_35, the inequality ψ(x)<1.03883x for x>0.
  • The separate Theorem 12 claim that ψ(x)/x attains its maximum at 113 is not part of this node.
    I plan to submit a separate solution for the maximum x=113 claim. Will try to assert that 1) it is a maximum, and 2) it is the ONLY maximum of ψ(x)/x
